title: Pilot GPU Sizing and Fallback Blueprint
content:
Executive summary:

Quick notes from workshop w/ customer-zetta on 2025-11-04. Goal: validate a pilot (4–8 week) dedicated capacity plan that meets 99thp latency SLOs (95% <= 150ms tail for short prompts, 95% <= 800ms for multi-turn chat up to 512 tokens) while keeping expected monthly GPU spend under $55k for stage env and $180k for production peak. This doc captures the sizing heuristics we used, a recommended autoscale + fallback policy, cost sensitivity scenarios, and an actionable runbook for the pilot phase.

Context / constraints: 
- Customer workload: real-time chat + occasional bulk embedding jobs. Peak concurrency observed in telemetry: 380 rps (chat inference requests), median request length 40 tokens, 10% long form (>256 tokens). Embedding batch jobs run nightly for 3 hours.
- Security: private deployment (VPC), KMS-managed keys, no external model bursting allowed without approval.
- Business need: demo must support 200 rps sustained at 95th percentile SLA; cost showed high sensitivity to GPU mix.

Workload profile used for sizing (derived from sample traces):
- Short-chat: 70% of requests, avg seq out+in ~64 tokens, target p50 latency <= 60ms p95 <= 150ms.
- Long-chat: 10% of requests, avg up to 512 tokens (generation), p95 target <= 800ms.
- Background embeddings: batches of 5k vectors, run in 3 hour window at night.
- Burst windows: 15 minute bursts up to 1.8x baseline rps, approx 30% probability per day.

Assumptions and conversion factors used: 
- Model family: Llama-2-like 13B quantized int8 opt path (on L4x). Throughput estimates: 1 L4x supports ~60 short-chat rps at 40-token workloads with 95% latency SLO. On A100-p4d (higher perf): ~150 short-chat rps at same config.
- Embedding throughput: A single A10/L4x can do ~40k embeddings/hr depending on batch size (batch-opt).
- Pricing: L4x @ $1.70/hr, A100-p4d equiv @ $7.20/hr (list estimates used for modeling).
- Cold start prewarm penalty: first request after node idle sees +120ms overhead unless prefix cache warmed.

Primary sizing recommendation (pilot cluster):
- Baseline compute: 6 x L4x nodes (reserved) for steady traffic handling (approx 6*60=360 short-chat rps capacity).
- Burst headroom: 2 x A100-sim nodes in a burst pool for up to 300 rps extra; autoscale to these nodes during sustained >1.3x baseline for >5 minutes.
- Embedding offload: 1 x dedicated A10-class node scheduled nightly (cron) for the embedding window; can be shared across tenants in pilot with strict quotas.
- Total pilot reserved hours estimate (monthly): (8 nodes * 24 * 30) = 5760 node-hours. Cost rough: (6*L4x*24*30*$1.70) + (2*A100*24*30*$7.20) amortized with burst factor ~0.15 = approx $22k/month base, $30–40k peak depending on burst usage and embedding runs. (Detailed sheet linked in artifacts.)

Autoscale policy (quantitative):
- Metric: short-chat RPS at 95th percentile of 1 minute windows.
- Scale-up triggers: when 95p RPS > (node_capacity * node_count * 0.85) sustained for 3 consecutive 60s windows -> add 1 node (L4x) to reserved pool, up to configured ceiling (12 L4x).
- Burst escalation: if after adding up to ceiling, 95p RPS > reserved_capacity * 0.9 for 2m -> spin up 1 A100-class node from burst pool (cooldown 180s). Max burst A100 nodes = 4.
- Scale-down triggers: if 95p RPS < (node_capacity * node_count * 0.50) for 10 consecutive min -> remove 1 node (min-reserved=4). Burst nodes scaled down after 15m idle by policy and draining active inference streams gracefully.
- Prewarm policy: maintain a minimum of 1 warm standby node for L4x to avoid cold start penalties. Keep KV/prefix cache snapshot for faster warmup when adding nodes.

Fallback policy (graceful degradation):
- First fallback (non-disruptive): route long-form requests to a quantized 7B variant (same family) when long queues detected; this reduces latency by ~40% but may reduce output quality for edge cases. Logged with tag: fallback:quant7b.
- Second fallback (regional): if burst pool exhausted and latency > SLO for >2 minutes, shift non-critical traffic to alternate region (subject to data residency rules). Requires pre-consent; only for pilot acceptance tests.
- Final fallback (throttle): soft-throttle tail requests, returning 503 with Retry-After headers for best-effort interactive clients. Use prioritized queuing: premium tokens > free trial tokens.

Cost sensitivity matrix (high level):
- Variable: % burst hours per month (0%, 5%, 20%). For 0% we estimate monthly compute $21k. At 5% burst -> $28k. At 20% burst -> $52k.
- Variable: embedding scheduling window length: increasing run from 3h -> 6h adds ~+$1.2k/mo if dedicated node kept live; if embedding shares compute opportunistically, delta < $400/mo but with higher job latency.
- Recommendation: negotiate committed reserved hours for pilot (monthly) at 10% discount; convert to dedicated commitment if pilot KPIs meet target.

Workshop decisions captured (actionable):
1) Customer agreed to pilot config: 6 L4x reserved, 2 A100 burst nodes, 1 embedding A10 node. (Action: SE to open provisioning ticket SE-4521; owner: Liam).
2) Add instrumentation hooks: token-level cost attribution, latency bracketing for short/long requests, fallback event counters. (Owner: Priya).
3) Run 3 scenario simulations (0%, 5%, 20% burst) using their trace with our sim harness and report back by 2025-11-11. (Owner: Diego).
4) Prepare customer-facing one-pager with tradeoffs and recommended fallback scripts for mobile SDKs. (Owner: Maya).

Runbook excerpt for pilot incident (tail latency spike):
- Step 0: Check 1m 95p RPS and node utilization. If utilization > 90% on all reserved nodes -> trigger scale-up via autoscaler manual override.
- Step 1: If autoscaler cannot provision burst nodes (quota failure) -> apply fallback: shift long-form requests to quant7b route and enable reduced token-budget for non-premium clients.
- Step 2: Communicate via status channel (customer slack) with templated message; include ETA (estimated 5–10m).

Open questions / risks:
- Quantized 13B on L4x assumptions need to be validated with customer's actual prompt distribution (we currently used sample 10k trace).
- Nightly embedding locality: if embeddings require stricter isolation, the shared A10 approach will not be acceptable; cost rises by ~2.5x if dedicated A100s required.
- SLA definition edge: the customer expects p99 in some internal docs — pilot currently built around p95. Need alignment.

Appendix (quick notes from bench runs):
- Bench run 2025-10-28: 1x L4x, short-chat 40-token workload -> observed 58 rps at 95p latency=140ms.
- Bench run 2025-10-30: 1x A100-sim -> observed 152 rps at 95p latency=120ms for same workload.
- Embedding bench 2025-11-01: A10-class node achieved 42k embeddings/hr w/ batch=128, 2.8ms/vec effective.

Meeting log / notes to self:
- Customer wants a clean upgrade path from pilot to reserved annual commitment; include soft opt-in for licensing discounts at 6 months.
- Slack thread: #cust-zetta-provision contains live questions re: KMS.
- Jira: SE-4521 (provisioning), SE-4527 (sim jobs), SE-4529 (fallback dev tasks).

Next steps (2-week sprint):
- Finish simulation runs and attach numeric cost curves.
- Implement fallback route prototype + unit tests.
- Prepare pilot acceptance checklist and runbook (customer signoff doc).

Notes: treat numbers as working estimates; update after sim runs. This doc is intentionally conversational; will convert to polished deck once sims validate numbers.
